analysis.title: The PunchLine, Issue 20: Spooky Stuff?
key_insights: Global markets are under strain as the Iran war, French political and fiscal turmoil, economic and fiscal stress and tech-sector anxiety converge. Global stocks have sold off and chipmakers have tumbled.
The Iran war has spread to Saudi Arabia, with a strike reported on Aramco and attacks on Riyadh airport. The Houthi militia has reportedly taken over leadership of Iran's regional 'Axis'.
The Iran war and shifts by China are tightening the supply of dollars in international markets, per the report.
US September PPI rose 1.3% m/m, the most since March 2022, vs 0.5% expected. Energy costs rose 10.8% on the Middle East war. Core PPI rose 0.7% m/m vs 0.3% forecast and 0.2% in August.

South Korea's KOSPI closed at a six-month low on Thursday. A chipmaker selloff triggered a circuit breaker after sticky US inflation data raised bets on further rate hikes and doubts about the AI investment boom.

Indonesian stocks fell 10.8% (660 points) to about 5,200 on Friday, a six-year low and the steepest one-day drop since January 1998. MSCI warned it could downgrade Indonesia to standalone market status. Goldman Sachs estimates up to $13B of outflows. MSCI's final decision is due by June 30, 2027.
French bond yields hit a 24-year high as unrest and a fiscal crisis collide. The report describes France as looking ungovernable and notes riots in which luxury retailers were looted.

Debt issued by AI infrastructure providers and neocloud companies has sunk toward stressed territory. Credit default swap volumes linked to big tech groups have soared as investors seek protection against an unraveling of the AI boom.

Big Tech has issued more than $429B in debt to fund the AI buildout. Gartner says AI data center owners need $8.5tn of revenue by end-2030 to cover capital and financing costs. The Financial Times reports at least 47 large US data center projects delayed, canceled or blocked in 2026.

The ASML CEO said AI demand will outstrip supply for years, after bumper profits well above analyst expectations. The BIS notes that a significant portion of AI financing and commercial relationships are self-referencing (circular financing).
US retail sales rose 0.8% m/m in September vs 0.3% expected, after an upwardly revised 1.3% in August. Gasoline station sales rose 6.4%, and ex-gas retail sales rose only 0.2%.
US industrial production rose 0.7% m/m in September vs 0.4% expected, the most in five months. Utilities rose 3.5%, manufacturing rose 0.3% (in line) and mining rose 0.2%.
The S&P Global US Composite PMI eased to 57.6 in October from 58.4 in September, still its second-highest level in over 5 years.

Housing is weak. Existing home sales were 3.99M annualized in September with 4.8 months of supply. Buyers canceled 14.5% of purchase contracts, the highest share on record outside the pandemic. Single-family starts were 859,000, down 4.6% from a revised 900,000.

China's September trade surplus widened to $133.5B from $88.7B a year earlier, vs $118.1B forecast, the largest since January 2025. Exports rose 36.3% y/y to $447.2B. The 2026 surplus is nearing $1 trillion.

China's domestic economy is weak. Property investment fell 20.6% y/y in January-September. FDI fell 4.3% y/y to USD 82.2B. Household consumption is stuck at 39% of GDP vs a 60% global norm. A demographer warns China's population may be overstated by up to 100 million.

The IMF raised its 2026 global growth forecast by 0.1pt to 3.1% (3.4% in 2027, from 3.5% in 2025). It flags high energy prices from the US-Iran war as a risk. US growth is 2.3% in 2026 and 2027, China 4.5% and 4.0%, Eurozone 1.1% and 1.2%, Japan 0.7%, India 7.0%.

Copper prices are near record levels on a threatened strike at Chile's La Escondida, the world's biggest copper mine. Other Chilean closures add to supply tightness, while AI data center and EV demand is strong.

Credit stress appears more widespread than default data indicate. Moody's says private credit risk assessments signal a 5.8% default rate. The IMF says zombie firms hold more than a fifth of Asia's corporate debt.
Healthcare costs are surging near 10%. Import air passenger fares rose 11.8% y/y. Food price warnings cite conflicts and one of the strongest El Niño events on record.

Commercial real estate: rising rates have derailed the property recovery, and transaction rebounds are being pushed into 2027. 2021-22 borrowers face 2027 refinancing deadlines. Manhattan office incentives top $90 per SF.
The Fed's financial stability view cited in the report flags elevated asset values, private credit growth and hedge fund activity as a possible source of Treasury market dislocation.
Saudi Arabia's oil exports are disrupted and its economy is projected to shrink 3.6% this year. Its flagship investor event is delayed to 2027. Private jet fees from Saudi Arabia are up 50%.

Debt has sunk toward stressed territory, CDS volumes on big tech are rising and circular financing is a concern.
Higher yields are derailing deals and pushing transactions into 2027, with refinancing pressure on 2021-22 vintage loans.
Prices are near record levels on supply disruption risk at La Escondida and demand from AI data centers and EVs.

earnings_insights: ASML reported bumper profits that far exceeded analyst expectations, per the report. No EPS or revenue figures are given.

risk_factors: Escalation of the Iran war in Saudi Arabia, disrupting oil exports.
French fiscal and political crisis with 24-year-high bond yields.
AI financing fatigue, circular financing and overbuilding, with neocloud and infrastructure debt near stressed levels.
Inflation re-acceleration (PPI +1.3% m/m) raising rate hike bets.
Hidden credit stress in private credit and Asian zombie firms.
MSCI downgrade of Indonesia to standalone status.
Chilean copper supply disruption from the La Escondida strike threat.
Food price shocks from conflicts and a strong El Niño.
Commercial real estate refinancing wall in 2027 and rate uncertainty.
China's weak domestic demand, property crash, demographics and possible data overstatement.
Cyber risk, including a web security flaw affecting about 70% of sites and AI-enabled scams.
vol_and_positioning: KOSPI hit a circuit breaker on a chipmaker selloff.
Credit default swap volumes linked to big tech groups have soared as investors seek protection against an AI boom unraveling.
Indonesian stocks had their steepest one-day drop since 1998, with up to $13B of outflows possible if MSCI downgrades the market (Goldman estimate).
geopolitical: The Iran war has spread to Saudi Arabia, with a strike on Aramco and attacks on Riyadh airport.
The Houthi militia has reportedly taken over leadership of Iran's regional 'Axis', and the Houthis are targeting Saudi cities.
Russia struck Ukrainian power plants hours after President Trump declared an energy ceasefire. European leaders warned of Russian escalation while the US pressed for Moscow-Kyiv talks.
China faces more trade barriers, and its export surge is likely to vex trade partners demanding it address imbalances.
Japan is months from running out of critical rare earths as China squeezes supply.
Unrest in France, including riots with looting of luxury retailers, and a fiscal crisis. A cyberattack hit refrigeration systems at 700 supermarkets, per the French government.
US midterm elections are approaching, with inflation pressuring voters.
cross_bank_references: Goldman Sachs estimates up to $13 billion of outflows if MSCI downgrades Indonesia.
Natixis analysts said state policies aided semiconductors' 'rapid development but not their profitability' (via the Financial Times).

tension_points.bull_case: ASML's CEO says AI demand will outstrip supply for years, and its profits far exceeded expectations. Big Tech continues to fund the buildout, and demand still exceeds supply.
tension_points.bear_case: Gartner says data center owners need $8.5tn of revenue by 2030. At least 47 US projects have been delayed or canceled. Neocloud debt is near stressed levels, and CDS volumes on big tech are soaring amid circular financing concerns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Financing fatigue and overbuilding, which the report says investors are watching for as more data-center financing comes.
